title: Data Structures and Algorithms in Java - Practice Exam Rubric

institution_context.target_students: FPT University students studying data structures and algorithms in Java
course_context: CSD-style practical algorithm and data structure implementation tasks
Tasks should stay within undergraduate coursework scope

easy.description: A direct implementation task using one clear data structure or one simple algorithmic idea.
expected_skills: Implement a straightforward array, loop, or single-structure operation.
should_avoid: Complex state management across multiple structures.

medium.description: A task requiring several coherent operations, moderate edge-case handling, or a clear algorithm/data-structure choice.
expected_skills: Implement and reason about a standard DSA task.
Write clean logic with meaningful test coverage.

hard.description: A substantial DSA task requiring algorithmic decomposition, careful edge-case handling, and stronger hidden-test coverage.
expected_skills: Choose or implement an appropriate algorithm or structure.
Provide a solution whose tests validate non-trivial behavior.
should_avoid: Topics not grounded in the chunks.

review_checks: The task must be grounded in the provided chunks.
The task must be genuinely about DSA concepts in Java course scope.
Difficulty must match implementation and reasoning effort.
skeleton_code must be coherent starter Java code.
solution_code must solve the stated problem correctly in principle.
test_cases must include visible validation and meaningful hidden checks.

easy: Requires non-trivial algorithm selection or many edge cases.
Needs deep reasoning about structure invariants.
Hidden tests imply much more than a direct practice task.
medium: Can be solved with one trivial pass and no real reasoning.
Requires advanced algorithm design far above normal course level.
Depends on unstated assumptions not grounded in the chunks.
hard: Only asks for a direct loop or one-step operation.
Contains weak or overly simple tests.
Does not require meaningful algorithmic thinking.

acceptance_rules: Accept only if the task, skeleton, solution, and tests are coherent and grounded.
Reject if the solution shape does not match the algorithmic task.
Reject if difficulty is inconsistent with the actual implementation burden.
regeneration_hints: Keep Easy tasks single-structure and direct.
Use explicit boundary handling for Medium tasks.
Reserve stronger decomposition and hidden coverage for Hard tasks.
